titulo.texto: The Altar of the Kings: The Golden Cave

frase_gancho.texto: The first altarpiece with estípite columns in Mexico, made between seventeen eighteen and seventeen thirty-seven.

puente_narrativo.texto: When you are ready, continue to the next stop on your tour.

guion_corto.texto: At the back of the church, behind the main altar, rises the Altar of the Kings. Jerónimo de Balbás made it between seventeen eighteen and seventeen thirty-seven, and the INAH considers it the first altarpiece made in Mexico with estípite columns. It is called the golden cave because of the glow of its gold leaf. It covers the head wall like a great carved wall, full of columns, images and ornaments. The fire of nineteen sixty-seven damaged its upper part, and it was restored afterward. Beneath this area lies the crypt of the archbishops. Look slowly: each level hides figures that reveal themselves with time.

guion_largo.texto:
You are standing before the largest and most dazzling work in the Cathedral. It occupies the back of the church, in the Main Chapel, behind the main altar, and for that reason it is also called the main altarpiece.

It is a creation of Jerónimo de Balbás. It was worked on between seventeen eighteen and seventeen thirty-seven, that is, for almost twenty years. It is said that another artist, Francisco Martínez, finished it after Balbás left. What matters is that the INAH considers it the first altarpiece made in Mexico with estípite pilasters, a support that grows thinner toward the bottom. After this altar, the estípite became very common in New Spain Baroque art.

The altar is made of white cedar and ayacahuite wood, covered with gold leaf. It measures about twenty-five meters high, almost fourteen wide and seven deep, figures that help you imagine its size. What you can see at a glance is that it fills the entire head wall, from bottom to top, leaving no free space.

Because of its glow it is known as the golden cave. It is a good image, because the altarpiece looks like a grotto of gold with niches, balconies and sculptures. Each level has niches with images. To read it calmly, begin at the bottom and rise with your gaze.

The altar suffered damage. On January 17, nineteen sixty-seven, the fire that began at the Altar of Forgiveness reached the upper part of this altarpiece. It was restored afterward. Today it is preserved as one of the greatest works of viceregal gilded carving.

It is also worth looking at what stands in front. The current main altar is a table, from the beginning of this century. It is a simple piece that contrasts with the ornate background. The table serves for today’s Mass, and the altarpiece keeps the memory of the worship of past centuries.

Beneath this area of the Cathedral lies the crypt of the archbishops. There rest Juan de Zumárraga, the first bishop of Mexico, and other archbishops from the city’s history. We will speak of it later.

Like many monuments in the city, this altar lives alongside the pre-Hispanic memory of the area. The Cathedral was built near the old Sacred Precinct, and the apse is at the north end of the church, far from the plaza. If you walk from here toward the east, leaving the Cathedral, within a few minutes you will reach the ruins of the Templo Mayor.

To finish, a piece of advice for viewing. Do not try to see the whole altarpiece at once. Begin at the base, go up level by level, and return to the center when you tire. This is a work that is best understood with time and without hurry.

texto: Start at the base of the altarpiece and climb with your eyes level by level
Count the estípites you can make out on the façade of the altarpiece
Look for the contrast between the simple main altar and the ornate altarpiece at the back

texto.Author: Jerónimo de Balbás
texto.Materials: white cedar and ayacahuite with gold leaf
texto.Approximate dimensions: about 25 m high, 13.75 m wide and 7.5 m deep
texto.Location: Main Chapel, north end of the church

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Altar of the Kings is made of solid gold.
texto.respuesta: Reality: It is a carved wooden altarpiece covered with gold leaf; that is why it is called the golden cave.
